title: Tenanted throttler degradation playbook and simulated failure exercises
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: We have seen intermittent client-facing latency and 429 spikes during partial limiter outages and during coordinated cross-region failovers. Existing mitigation behavior (aggressive fail-open with best-effort policing) reduces latency but causes fairness regressions and increased tail-error surface for tenants with bursty workloads. Goals: 1) Define an operational playbook for deterministic, tenant-aware degraded-mode behavior when primary limiter control plane is unavailable; 2) Implement a simulation harness to validate playbook under realistic multi-region traffic patterns and KV lease churn; 3) Produce SLO-safe fallback defaults and per-tenant configurable policies (grace window, guaranteed-minimum-share, soft-credits); 4) Ship runbook and automated chaos tests to prevent regressions. Scope: This ticket drives design, experiments, and runbook creation; separate follow-ups will implement tenant UI and billing-side telemetry. Non-goals: wholesale redesign of quotas; upstream protocol changes. Background: Past incidents (incident-redwood-2025-11-07, partial_limiter_outage) pointed to two failure modes: 1) control-plane partition where regional limiter nodes retain inconsistent lease views causing short-term double-allocation; 2) catastrophic limiter OOMs leading to flappy admission where clients oscillate between allowed/denied and produce retry storms. Both cases interact poorly with multi-region failover (requests switch region -> different limiter state). This ticket focuses on deterministic mitigations and measurable SLO impact assessments.
acceptance_criteria: A documented playbook describing step-by-step operator actions for: detection, safe-fallback activation, tenant notification, rollback and postmortem data collection.

A simulation harness (k6 + local traffic generator) that can replay recorded tenant traffic patterns and inject: lease-loss, delayed heartbeats, and region blackholing. Tests produce reproducible metrics and assertions.

A candidate degraded-mode implementation (configurable via flags) that demonstrates: proportional soft-share allocation, grace-window allowance for short bursts, and deterministic circuit-breaker thresholds with hysteresis.

Baseline SLO impact analysis comparing current behavior vs candidate degraded-mode across three tenant archetypes (steady, bursty, spiky) with charts/output stored in the reliability-dashboard linked in comments.
Runbook committed to /confluence/infra/limiter-degraded-playbook with checklist and postmortem template; two on-call engineers have run the playbook in a tabletop exercise.
tech_notes: Degraded-mode design: local per-node soft-credit pool + deterministic shard-based proportional allocation. Nodes maintain ephemeral baseline credits (configurable percent of steady-state) to avoid abrupt all-or-nothing denial.

Circuit-breaker policy: switch to degraded-mode when >25% of limiter instances report memory pressure OR >15% request admission variance across replicas for 60s window. Exit degraded-mode after 120s of stable metrics.

Fairness heuristic: use tenant-weighted rolling-average of RPS over T=5min to compute guaranteed-min-share; apply fast-path for tenants below small-tenant threshold to avoid starving noise-level traffic.
KV lease consistency: introduce short-lived tombstones with monotonic epoch to allow replays to detect double-allocation windows during partition heal; simulation will validate tombstone correctness.

Metrics/telemetry: add limiter.node.degraded_mode_active boolean, limiter.node.soft_credit_utilization, limiter.tenant.provisioned_share_estimate, limiter.admissions.rejection_reasons histogram; hook to SLA dashboards.
Observability: correlation ids for fallback activations and per-request sampling to trace cross-region failovers into admission outcomes. Dashboards must surface per-tenant SLO delta vs expected.
Safety: default to conservative degraded quotas for enterprise tier with explicit override flags; fail-open only for internal health-check routes.
